claim_as_stated: There exist a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group G, an injection i:Z²→G, and c∈H²(BG;Z) with <(Bi)*c,[T²]>=1 while i*(β)=0 in K₀(C*rG), for the rank-zero Bott generator β. Hence the pushed torus Dirac class has infinite order in K₀(BG) but zero coefficient-free reduced assembly image; finite presentation is not claimed.
proof_architecture: Build a finite-alphabet layered graph with two-evaluation finite-field recovery, causally keyed permutation tables and lagged padded-tail gates. A conditional Fourier estimate gives centered mean norm <3/5. Matchings, cut concentration and a local-lemma selection give every undeleted incidence a fixed gap while increasing probabilities of joint current-table tests by at most exp(ε_s k).

Prune minimal coherent returns and short bicycles. Formal reconstruction fixes all current inputs before exposing tables; a predictable accumulated-rank process charges compatibility bits without conditioning on future minimality. Terminal and branch tests are charged at disjoint updates. Small deletion retains girth and excludes short Heisenberg laws; a Heisenberg law forces a bicycle each of whose edges is traversed at least four times.

Use compact Bott profiles near the golden-ratio torus coordinate, spread over disjoint Heisenberg translates with tiny trace carriers, and sample a finite Fourier envelope by independent diffuse horizontal coordinates plus bounded matrix weights. Polynomial avoidance gives short voltage girth, while base girth, finite Følner-box norm tests and centered moments give full regular norm approximation under the same independent edge law.

Private completion and finite diagram curvature embed the voltage cover and Heisenberg subgroup. Fixed-contact polygon bounds permit finite peeling of sheets, direct cycle coordinates and compactness-selected disjoint domains with residual forest. Exact cone chains exclude prime torsion and extend an explicit integral Heisenberg 2-cocycle evaluating −1 on the (z,x) torus.

Small carrier trace controls trimming and untrimmed synthesis. Finite Cayley formulas, spectral constant extraction and a residual-forest norm bound realize fixed-size Bott families and uniform paths in a norm sequence quotient. Even→odd→positive-even homotopies and finite additivity cancel the root class; supported transport identifies it with the physical torus Bott class. Fixed stabilization and corner normalization recover eventual exact equality in one reduced algebra.

Choose parameters in a noncircular order and extract a finitely generated subgroup from one finite K-theory witness, retaining the embedded torus. Restrict the negative detector class and pair its line bundle with the torus Dirac class to obtain index 1. Subgroup naturality identifies its reduced assembly with the zero Bott class, producing the claimed infinite-order kernel.

claim_as_stated: Every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable finite-dimensional topological manifold without boundary is a Lie group. The central claimed result excludes faithful continuous Z_p actions for every prime and dimension; every such Z_p action therefore factors through a finite quotient.
proof_architecture: Define T(X) from proper continuous images of constants on compact finite polyhedra, together with shifts, cones, and summands; prove Verdier duality on the actual generated categories using simplex generators. A symmetric interval-cone construction proves homotopy invariance of degree-r Witt groups E_r(X).

Cut off finite source constructions to identify quotient morphisms with germs. Apply integral Witt localization. For a full dense triangulated inclusion, explicitly double a form with a hyperbolic stabilization to build reverse maps whose two composites are multiplication by 2.

Compare semialgebraic and continuous categories on pole covers of spheres using finite exact diagram chases. Obtain a fixed exponent e_j with e₀=0 and e_j=9e_{j−1}+6. A local signature on a ball for each finite relation proves the semialgebraic rational sphere generator is integral, so the continuous rational line has denominator bounded by L_d=2^{e_d}, fixed before the action partition.

Assuming a faithful Z_p action, use Newman's rigidity to find a faithful orientation-preserving action in a chart; stabilize to odd d>n. Average a compactly supported pinch to get a fixed degree-one sphere test through the orbit space. Faithfulness supplies p^k local finite-quotient sheets. Rational orbit pullback plus odd-sphere telescopes move a positive-degree multiple of the test into those sheets.

Partition p-primary characters into m=p^k cyclic classes. Construct their integral Witt classes from α and α(2e_i−1) in a quotient, avoiding splitting quotient idempotents. A matrix congruence proves the sum is 2[A]. Local sheet multipliers make the concentrated classes equal; covariance and homotopy imply the original rational classes are equal after cancelling a nonzero degree scalar.

The original integral classes remain in the fixed lattice and sum rationally to 4u_d, so each equals (4/m)u_d. Choose m>4L_d to force 0<4L_d/m<1 to be an integer. This excludes Z_p; the classical Hilbert–Smith reduction yields the stated Lie-group theorem.

The fixed denominator depends strongly on the chosen odd sphere dimension. It is fixed before m=p^k, not uniform in dimension.

title: A positive solution to Tingley’s problem
scope_note: Full pinned source closure read: README, all 544 lines of the one-file manuscript including embedded chord diagram and fixed-point appendix, and all 151 lines of the references include. Initial output truncation was repaired by explicit line-range rereads. The PDF was not separately rendered; reading is not validation.
claim_as_stated: For any nonzero real Banach spaces X,Y and surjective sphere isometry f:S_X→S_Y, the radial map T(0)=0 and T(x)=||x||f(x/||x||) is the unique surjective real-linear isometric extension. No finite-dimensionality, separability, reflexivity, smoothness, or strict convexity hypothesis is imposed; for complex spaces the claim concerns real linearity.
proof_architecture: Define D_q(x,y)=||f(x)−qf(y)||−||x−qy|| and its absolute supremum M. The defect is uniformly 2-Lipschitz in q, bounded by 2min(q,1−q), and changes sign under inversion. If M>0, choose maximizing sequences and pass to an ultrapower and completion so a positive maximum is attained at one 0<t<1 while every pair/radius retains the bound M.

Take opposite radial contacts through ty and tf(y) to define a continuous return map g on directions. Equality at maximal defect forces r=u+M, s=p+M, and a common support for v and g(v). Common-support propagation builds a nonempty invariant closed convex set contained in the maximizing directions.

Show ||g(v)−g(v′)||≤up/(rs)||v−v′|| plus two errors in scalar radii. Since up/(rs)≤(1−M/(1+t))²<1, partition the bounded scalar-radius ranges into finitely many bins to obtain strict contraction of Kuratowski noncompactness. Darbo gives a fixed direction, aligning both extremal chords with p+r=s+u≤2.

For aligned chords define A=p/d,B=u/d,ε=1−t. Weighted signed defects cancel the same target norm and produce a secant K with ε/p≤φ(v)≤K≤1−B or B. If either A or B exceeds ε, support signs and inverse symmetry give a small radial perturbation that makes the defect exceed M.

In the remaining regime A,B≤ε, original and inverse secant bounds imply ε≤dA(1−B), ε≤dB(1−A), and ε<1/2. Convexity gives incompatible bounds on the same preserved distance ||y−z||=||f(y)−f(z)||. Thus M=0.

Zero defect makes the radial map an onto metric isometry. The included Mazur–Ulam midpoint-reflection proof doubles any midpoint error while retaining a uniform bound, forcing additivity and then real homogeneity. The appendix proves the noncompactness lemmas, simplex fixed point via Sperner parity, compact convex fixed point, and Darbo.

Explicitly record which determinant, ordering, and sign convention remain common. The paper's formula is a norm identity, so no determinant inequality follows without a new identity.

limits: Full source reading does not independently validate the novel alignment, invariant convex set, return-map estimate, or secant contradiction.

The proof uses real Banach geometry, convexity, supports, arbitrary enlargements, and continuous fixed-point methods. Integer transversals and determinants do not automatically satisfy these hypotheses.
A sphere isometry supplies exact distance equalities and an inverse with the same defect bound; these are substantial structural hypotheses unavailable from a generic occupancy model.
Ultrapower attainment and continuous fixed points can discard finite arithmetic information. They cannot by themselves yield a nonzero integer determinant or a BA/non-BA conclusion for π.
